tagline.text: A coconut plantation where you dip your feet in waterfall water while eating lunch

location.label: Location
location.text: Tiaong, Quezon Province (bordering San Pablo, Laguna)

items.credit: National Historical Commission of the Philippines / Public domain / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A coconut plantation cultivated by one family since the late 19th century, turned into a resort where in a single day you can enjoy a Filipino buffet lunch at bamboo tables with your feet dipped in water below a waterfall, along with a private museum, carabao-cart rides, and folk dance performances.
Villa Escudero is an approximately 800-hectare coconut plantation resort straddling the border of Tiaong, Quezon Province and San Pablo, Laguna, at kilometer
91km
of the Maharlika Highway. The Escudero family started it as a sugarcane plantation in the
s before switching to coconuts, and opened it to the general public from the early
s. The plantation is still actually in operation today, so the old rural Philippine scenery of carabao (water buffalo) pulling carts among endless rows of palm trees remains just as it was.

What made this place famous nationwide is the "Waterfall Restaurant." Bamboo tables are set just below a shallow waterfall spilling over the Labasin Dam, and guests dip their feet in the cool, ankle-deep water while eating Filipino food served on banana leaves. The sight of white water cascading behind the tables has appeared for decades, without fail, in postcards and travel guides introducing the Philippines.

The Escudero family museum inside the resort is also worth seeing. Housed in a pink building resembling a Spanish colonial-era church, it's packed with the family's collection of religious icons (santos), silver altar ornaments, old coins and stamps, war relics, folk costumes, and taxidermy, and is known as one of the largest private collections in the Philippines.

With almost no physical demands and every activity contained within one compound, it especially suits trips with parents in tow, families with young children, and Korean expats hosting visitors from home. Unlike a flashy beach resort, it's a place to experience a slow, warm day of Philippine country life.

The highlight of the day tour. With your feet dipped in the waterfall water, enjoy a Filipino buffet of adobo, grilled fish, pancit, and tropical fruit. The water is cold and the floor is slippery, so aqua shoes are handy.
Ride a cart pulled by water buffalo from the entrance to the plaza deep in the plantation. A local band riding along plays old Filipino songs on guitar and bandurria.
An enormous collection is on display, from religious icons and sacred art to colonial-era household items and souvenirs gathered from around the world. It's worth about
30–40 minutes
to tour with a guide's commentary.
A folk dance performance choreographed by National Artist Ramon Obusan, featuring regional traditional dances such as tinikling, where dancers hop between clapping bamboo poles.
Ride a bamboo raft along the Bulakin River, drifting slowly past palm-lined banks. Perfect for an unhurried afternoon outing.
The day tour includes use of the swimming pool, and a walk along the plantation trails lets you see how coconuts are processed.

children.text: The scene of a bahay kubo (traditional bamboo house), a carabao, and palm trees comes even more alive in photos if you're dressed in traditional Filipino clothing.

If staying overnight, check in during the afternoon and take a sunset walk around the plantation, then enjoy the falls and riverside without crowds early the next morning before moving on to Pagsanjan Falls or the San Pablo lakes.
From Manila, take SLEX down toward Calamba and Santo Tomas, pass through San Pablo town, and follow the Maharlika Highway toward Tiaong. It's about
90km
and takes
2–3 hours
; you can also go via the STAR Tollway through Lipa and San Pablo. Toll costs are about
one way.
From Buendia, Cubao, or PITX, take a bus (DLTB, JAC Liner, Jam Liner, etc.) bound for Lucena and ask to be let off at "Villa Escudero entrance." It takes about
2.5–3.5 hours
, with fares around
. From the entrance it's about a
5–10 minute
walk to the resort reception. For the return trip, flag down a Manila-bound bus on the road in front of the entrance.
Packages combining Manila hotel pickup with a day-tour ticket are sold for about
per person. With a small group, this cuts down on transport costs and can be more economical.
The best season is the dry season,
November–May
December–February
in particular is cool with almost no rain, making dining at the Waterfall Restaurant pleasant.
March–May
has hot midday temperatures, but the cool waterfall water actually makes it even more popular.
During the wet season (
June–October

), if it rains or the river rises, lunch is served at an indoor restaurant instead of the Waterfall Restaurant for safety. This can mean missing the day tour's key experience, so during the wet season it's best to check the forecast before picking a date. Raft operations may also be suspended right after a typhoon.
In nearby Lucban, Quezon Province, the Pahiyas Festival is held around
May 15
each year, when houses are decorated with rice wafers and farm produce. If you visit around
mid-May
, it's a great chance to combine the two destinations in one trip. Weekends, public holidays, and Holy Week draw large tour groups, so a weekday visit is recommended.

Accommodation inside the resort consists of rooms in the style of traditional bamboo-and-wood houses and riverside cottages. The nightly rate usually includes meals and resort activities, running about

for two. Some rooms have air conditioning, but the atmosphere is rural, with frogs and insects audible at night, so don't expect a quiet city-style hotel. To cut costs, you can stay at a budget-to-midrange hotel (about
a night) in San Pablo town, about
20–30 minutes
away by car.

Lunch at the Waterfall Restaurant is a Filipino home-style buffet featuring chicken adobo, grilled tilapia, pancit canton, lumpia, rice, and tropical fruit such as bananas and mangoes. There's almost nothing spicy, so it suits children's palates well too.

For food nearby, buko pie along the highway through San Pablo and Los Baños is famous, and it's also well worth trying longganisa (garlicky sausage) and pancit habhab, eaten by hand off a banana leaf, in Lucban, Quezon. And being a coconut plantation, fresh buko juice (young coconut water) is a must.
It's safest to book the day tour in advance through the official online shop (shop.villaescudero.com). On weekends and public holidays, walk-in tickets can sell out early.
Operating hours are usually
8 AM to 5 PM
. Activities after entry can be done in any order, but the cultural show runs only at set times, so check the schedule when you enter.
If you get to the Waterfall Restaurant before half past
, there are fewer people and photos come out clean. After
, it gets crowded with tour groups.
Shorts, sandals, or aqua shoes are comfortable to wear. Your clothes can get wet from the waterfall, so bring a change of clothes.
Some areas inside the museum restrict photography. Follow the posted instructions and don't use flash.
Seniors and persons with disabilities qualify for the legally mandated discount, but proof is required, and if you book online you may need to contact the reservations team separately.
Both cash and cards are accepted, but the small shops on the plantation often take cash only.
If you're coming by bus, check the last return departure time in advance. Once the sun sets, it gets harder to flag down a bus on the road by the entrance.

The floor of the Waterfall Restaurant is very slippery because of moss. Elderly visitors should always hold someone's hand when moving around, and keep an eye on children so they don't run around in the water.
On days with heavy rain, the waterfall meal may be cancelled for safety, and in that case it's usually replaced with an indoor meal rather than a refund.
Carabao are gentle animals, but they can be startled if you suddenly approach or touch them from behind. Follow the staff's instructions when riding the cart.
There are a lot of mosquitoes around the plantation. Especially at dusk, bring long clothing and insect repellent to guard against dengue.
The Maharlika Highway has heavy truck traffic. Take extra care when getting off a bus or crossing the road.
